models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Very light, slack pattern over the Aeolians right now - 1-6 kt and near-flat seas - but it is far too early to call the trip days.
briefing.synopsis: No organised gradient over the islands: the ECMWF/ICON consensus sampled every 6 h shows wind at Lipari, Panarea, Stromboli, Filicudi and Salina running roughly 1-6 kt with gusts mostly 5-14 kt, and the direction swinging through the compass between each sample - the signature of a sea-breeze/land-breeze regime under weak synoptic forcing rather than any mistral or scirocco. Wave and swell heights sit at 0.1-0.6 ft everywhere in the payload. Through 1-3 Oct the models keep that pattern going, with a nightly southerly land breeze at Portorosa (around 5 kt from 182-207 degrees) flipping to N/NW by midday. The payload gives me no pressure-centre analysis, so I am describing the wind field itself rather than naming a system.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: For the first night at Portorosa (3 Oct) the recommendation is Portorosa Marina - an enclosed basin with all-round shelter, and the only option listed, so the choice does not matter. ECMWF-based consensus for that date gives SE 3.8 kt, gusts 8.4 kt, swell 0.1 ft. Nothing in the payload would push the fleet elsewhere; that would change only if a real gradient appeared in later runs.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: We are still two days out, so there is no departure window to lock in tonight. As the data stands, Portorosa to Lipari on 4 Oct is flagged go at every window from 06:00 to 14:00, with a recommended 06:00 start giving SSE 5.4 kt, gusts 11.9 kt and 0.1 ft seas for a 22 nm run - essentially a motoring morning. Treat that as a pattern indication only; it is a reflection of the current regime, not a forecast you should plan around yet.

passage_notes.note: Go at all windows. 06:00 gives SSE 5.4 kt, gusts 11.9 kt, 0.1 ft - a dead run that will be motoring. Wind backs to NNE by midday at 3-5 kt.
Go throughout. 2.5-4.0 kt, NE early then NW/NNW, 0.1 ft. 06:00 is head to wind at 2.6 kt - motor.
Go at all windows, 2.5-4.6 kt and 0.1 ft. Note Marina del Gabbiano is rated only workable, open from every direction, with no anchoring - it depends entirely on it staying calm.

passage_notes.leg: Stromboli → Panarea, optional return (6 Oct, 11 nm)
passage_notes.note: Go throughout. NNE 4.5-6.2 kt, gusts to 10.5, seas 0.3-0.5 ft - a short downwind hop.
Go at all windows and the breeziest leg in the set: S/SSW 5.5-7.0 kt, gusts to 13.8 kt, 0.7-0.9 ft. This is at the very end of the forecast horizon (07 Oct 23:00) - low value as a plan.

cautions: Everything in the payload is benign - this is a light-air, flat-water pattern with no listed caution or no-go window. The honest risk here is complacency, not weather.
Lead time, not conditions, is the issue: the legs run 4-7 Oct and the data only reaches 07 Oct 23:00, so the later legs are single-run glimpses that will change.

Where the models already disagree they disagree widely in light air: at Lipari 06:00 on 1 Oct the spread is 1.8-8.7 kt and at Panarea the same hour 3.3-9.8 kt. Treat consensus means in this regime as indicative only.
Marina del Gabbiano at Stromboli (5 Oct) is exposed through 360 degrees and anchoring is not permitted - shelter there holds only while it stays calm, so keep the Panarea option live.
ECMWF IFS gusts are interval maxima, so the large gust-to-mean ratios in 2-3 kt air (for example 6.8 kt over a 2 kt mean on the Lipari leg) are a model artefact, not a squall signal.
briefing.confidence_note: Run-to-run wind-speed stability is good - mean shift only 0.7 kt at 72-120 h lead across 23 snapshots - but mean direction shifts of 48-64 degrees at the same leads, plus the 6+ kt model spreads already showing at Lipari and Panarea, mean the strength signal is more trustworthy than the direction, and the trip dates themselves sit at or beyond the useful horizon.

verification.measures: forecast stability, not verified accuracy - the reference is the newest model run for the same hour, not an observation
